Twenty-six comments

Garry Kennedy’s Delight (as recorded by Celtic Tradition in 1984)

This tune was recorded by the group Celtic Tradition (feat. Noel McLoughlin):
LP Celtic Tradition “I Have Waited for Many a Night and Day”, released in 1984 by Maske Music GmbH, Germany.

It appears as a set of reels entitled “Easter Sunday/Garrykennedy’s Delight” (spelling exactly as printed). However, Easter Sunday is the *second* tune of the set, so I assume “Garrykennedy’s Delight” applies to the first one, which I submit here (I allowed myself to separate “Garry” and “Kennedy’s”). Both tunes are indicated as traditional.

I couldn’t find any info about this group (imagine googling “celtic tradition” ;-) ). The recording has apparently never been released on a CD (even the vinyl LP was not easy to find). It seems that the group has had little or no commercial success. Which is a pitty, as this is one of my favourite recordings of Irish music!

↳ Posted by macaileacs on October 19th, 2008.

Garrykennedy

Garrykennedy is a place in Tipperary and the tune “Garrykennedy Castle” was a composition by the Late Paddy O’Brien from Nenagh. I wouldn’t know about this tune though but the name seems to be a bit of a coincidence and it might be another of Paddy’s.

I suspected it was a software splat. Some of the ABC software throws up ABC notation like vomit, identifiable pieces but a mess… Yeah, so you had a Vindaloo and ~ there were raisins in it… :-P

If I had the recording I’d send you a clearer transcription… It helps to know and understand ABC notation longhand, also because some software is dated and temperamental, even though ABC notation predates the software and computers, including the simpler forward slash / rather than /2, which indicate the same thing, the halving in time value of the note before it…

Paddy O’Brien tune
There is another G reel in the data base that is titled The Primrose Lasses and is sub-titled Patrick’s Night. I have never heard Primrose Lasses called by any other name. It is a lovely tune but has little relation to this tune.

This Patrick’s Night is the reel composed by Nenagh’s Paddy O’Brien, and is played by Kitty Hayes, among many others. It is similar is many ways to Touch Me If You Dare and is often played in the same set, the theory being that tunes that are similar should be played back-to-back to keep the differences in mind.
